title: How can a protractor measure an angle wider than a straight angle?
description: The marked angle in the book is wider than a straight angle, so the protractor cannot read it directly. The unmarked angle is measured instead, and it is taken away from a full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: the marked angle and the unmarked angle together make a full turn of 360 degrees. Watch for students who try to read the marked angle straight off the scale.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q4
video_script.why: The child measures the unmarked angle by the three checks of the solved example, and takes it away from a full turn to get the marked angle.
video_script.substitution: The marked and unmarked angles of the book's drawing.
video_script.anchor: the book's drawing of an angle with the outside marked and the inside unmarked
video_script.payoff_line: The marked angle measures two hundred and sixty degrees
maths_rules: a protractor reads only up to 180 degrees
a full turn is 360 degrees, so marked angle = 360 - 100 = 260 degrees
video_script.design: The drawing stays on the board. The protractor measures the inside angle only, and the subtraction from the full turn is held back until the answer line.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>How could we still find the measure of the marked angle?

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Step one, see that the protractor stops at one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The marked angle runs on past the end of the scale, so we cannot read it directly.

narration: <bookmark mark='measure'/>Step two, measure the unmarked angle.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>Put the centre on the vertex, one arm on the zero line, and read from that zero.
<bookmark mark='read'/>It reads one hundred degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, take the unmarked angle away from the full turn.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>What is left is the marked angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check that the marked angle is more than 180° and that the two angles add up to 360°

narration: <bookmark mark='wider'/>Step four, check the answer. The marked angle must be wider than a straight angle.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The two angles must add up to a full turn.

marks.ans: the subtraction is written and the result is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three hundred and sixty minus one hundred is two hundred and sixty.
The marked angle measures two hundred and sixty degrees.
